# folders

Live file listings of watched folders.

```lua
local folder = (os.getenv("HOME") or "") .. "/Pictures/Wallpapers"
mantle.folders:watch(folder, { "jpg", "png" })

list {
    items = mantle.folders:map(function(folders)
        local listing = folders.watched[folder]
        return listing and listing.entries or {}
    end),
    key = function(entry) return entry.path end,
    each = function(entry)
        return text { content = entry.name }
    end,
}
```

## State

`mantle.folders:get()` returns `FoldersState`, `nil` before the first push. A field marked `?` may be absent.

`mantle.folders` payload.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `watched` | `table<string, Folder>` | One entry per `"watch"`, keyed by its absolute `path` (`~/` expanded) minus trailing slashes; `nil` until watched. |

### `FileEntry`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modified` | `integer` | Modification time in Unix seconds; `0` when unavailable. |
| `name` | `string` | File name, e.g. `"sunrise.jpg"`. |
| `path` | `string` | Absolute path. |

### `Folder`

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` | `FileEntry[]` | Files (and symlinks to files) directly inside, minus dotfiles, filtered by extension and sorted case-insensitively by name. Relisted 200 ms after the last change. |
| `error?` | `string` | Why listing failed, e.g. `"No such file or directory (os error 2)"`; `nil` on success. A missing or deleted folder keeps this error until it appears, then lists on its own. |
| `ready` | `boolean` | `false` until the first listing lands, then `true` even when empty or failed. |

## Actions

Call each as `mantle.folders:<action>(arguments...)`; `?` marks an argument you may omit.

| Action | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `watch` | `path: string, extensions?: string[]` | Keeps `watched[path]` listing a folder, absolute or `~/` under `$HOME`. `extensions` match case-insensitively, dot optional; omitted means every file. |
| `unwatch` | `path: string` | Stops watching `path` (absolute or `~/`) and removes it from `watched`. |

## Backend

One inotify watch per folder, on the folder only: subfolders are neither listed nor watched. A new
generation drops every watch, so call `watch` at top level and each evaluation asks again; repeating
a `watch` with the same `extensions` only re-pushes the listing.

A missing folder is watched through its nearest existing ancestor: `ready` is `true` with `error`
set until the folder appears, then it lists with `error` cleared. A watched folder that is deleted
or moved away does the same, and lists again when it comes back.

## Gotchas

| Trap | Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| `watched["~/Pictures"]` is `nil` after `watch("~/Pictures")` | `watched` is keyed by the expanded absolute path: `watched[os.getenv("HOME") .. "/Pictures"]` |
| `watched[path]` is `nil` after a `watch` | The key drops trailing slashes: `watch("/walls/")` lands at `watched["/walls"]` |
| `error` is set but the folder exists | It is set while the folder is missing and clears on the next listing, up to 200 ms after the folder appears |

See also: [`process.run`](../guide/processes.md#processrun) to read a file's contents.
